gap: No result ChatGPT got states that only one of its four picks, the Aoocci F5 ($189 at aoocci.com on 2026-11-14), can run without wiring to the bike. Carpuride says the W702 Plus/W702S Plus USB-C port cannot power the unit and burns it out above 5 V, and Chigee's AIO-5 power cable must go to the battery's +, − and ACC terminals.
standout_why: ThrottleBuff (2026-11-04) has no prices, battery capacities or runtimes. It gives a general 5 V/2.5 A (12.5 W) need and a 4–6 h phone-drain figure, and it says most units wire to 12 V, which is part of this finding. MotorcycleGPSHub (2026-11-11) also has no battery or runtime figures, recommends Chigee's 12 V/1 A harness, and quotes Carpuride's 4.5 V/2.5 A USB minimum. I could not read Handlebar HQ's list page (SSL certificate error), so I could not check it. None of the pages I read gives a runtime per charge, hours on a power bank, or cost per riding hour for any screen. I could not source the derived number myself (the F5's hours per charge), so all this angle adds is which units need wiring and today's prices.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's 'best for portability' pick. Of the units checked, the F5 is the only one sold as wire-free. Carpuride's W702 Plus/W702S Plus warn that their USB-C port cannot power the unit, and Chigee's AIO-5 power cable wires to the battery's +, − and ACC terminals, so these are fixed installs, not portable units. ChatGPT's $199 for the F5 and $279.99 for the W702 are both above today's store prices. The derived figure that would decide it, the F5's ride-hours per charge and cost per hour, is still unsourced.
